name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 15 points
Incumbent Scanlon running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 98%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively to Scanlon: a D+15 district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of over $1.2 million raised versus about $21,000 for Manganaro, who has no outside backing. Markets agree, pricing her near 98%, so the forecast stays at a Safe D with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or a sharply unfavorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Mary Gay Scanlon seeks another term in a Delaware County-area district that leans Democratic by about 15 points. She has raised more than $1.2 million and holds roughly $460,000 on hand, while Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised about $21,000 with minimal cash and no visible outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put her chances near 98%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the main question being the size of the winning margin rather than who wins.
